page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-8 is an ARM-based virtual machine instance powered by an 8-core ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 processor. Operating at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz, it features 8 dedicated vCPUs with a single thread per physical core. The instance is configured with 64 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It lacks local storage and bundled GPUs, and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong memory performance, with the Passmark memory score ranking in the top 10% and large-block read-only memory bandwidth reaching 200.21 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25%. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks also perform in the top 25%, with gzip compression at 32.23 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.36 GB/sec. However, the instance exhibits weaker performance in cryptographic operations, with the Passmark CPU encryption test falling into the bottom 25%.

While the instance delivers average performance for general-purpose tasks like static web serving and Redis operations, it is less suited for heavy cryptographic workloads or larger language model inference, as demonstrated by a weak prompt processing speed of 19.53 tokens/sec on 7B models. Given its high memory density and strong memory bandwidth, the c4a-highmem-8 is well-suited for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, and text processing tasks that do not require local storage or GPU acceleration.
